end.summary:
Practised drawing dot pictures for square and triangular numbers.
Used rows and columns to show how a sequence grows.
Explained that the shared corner is counted twice, so one dot is subtracted.
Initially mixed up 12 + 13, then corrected the total to 25 using the shared-corner method.
Ended by finding the jump from 5² to 6² as 11 dots; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Ishita practised representing square and triangular numbers with dot pictures and explaining sequence growth through rows and columns. They clearly explained the shared-corner method: count the new row and column, then subtract one because the corner was counted twice. There was an initial mix-up with 12 + 13, and it was corrected later in the lesson using the picture. At home, ask them to draw 5×5 and 6×6 dot squares and circle the 11 dots added when growing from one to the next.
